subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global agent dry-run mode, and which execution surfaces must be covered before users can trust it as a safety boundary?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but it cannot choose whether adapter-only interception is acceptable or whether Gateway, client-hosted, external CLI-backend, hook, approval, and logging semantics must be included from day one.

options.title: Design the safety contract first
options.body: Specify supported surfaces, preview/result shape, sensitive-parameter redaction, and unsupported-surface behavior before implementing the flag.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Track this under the Ask/Plan/Modify direction while preserving this issue as the focused requirement for tool-call preview semantics.

options.title: Decline global interception
options.body: Keep per-command dry-runs, tool policy, and approval hooks as the supported safety mechanisms, then close this direction after maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design the safety contract first
recommendation.body: Specify supported surfaces, preview/result shape, sensitive-parameter redaction, and unsupported-surface behavior before implementing the flag.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal for central agent execution and CLI runner behavior points to this owner for the product/security boundary decision.
